newsitem.title: USA: Columbus to use new Ohio TIF law for bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Columbus to use new Ohio TIF law for bond issue.

text.p: Columbus, Ohio, plans to use a new state law to divert funds from a tax increment financing district to help back bonds for a road project not in the district, according to city officials.

Wyatt Kingseed, Columbus' finance director, said the city would probably use TIF revenues as well as income tax revenues for a possible general obligation bond issue to fund the city's portion of a downtown connector road.

That project is estimated to cost $200 million, with Columbus' share of the costs pegged at about $42 million, according to city figures. State and federal sources are expected to pay for the bulk of the project.

The use of TIF revenues was made possible by a provision in a bill signed into law by Gov. George Voinovich on Monday. That provision allows one Ohio city to use revenues from a TIF district to fund a public improvement outside of the district.
Pat Grady, Columbus' economic development administrator, said the city plans to pass the required ordinance to take advantage of the provision by yearend.
Grady added that incremental property tax revenues the city would use from the yet-to-be-created TIF district would not include any school taxes.

The sponsor of the bill originally wanted to allow all Ohio cities to divert TIF revenues for other public improvements. However, the provision was eventually watered down to one city, with the expectation that Columbus would take advantage of the law, according to a legislative aide.
Kingseed said Columbus might be used as a test case to see how it works.
